1.meaning: By the Mount — an oath sworn by Mount Sinai (Ṭūr Sīnāʾ), the sacred mountain where Moses received revelation. The wāw is the oath-wāw.
1.grammar: A proper noun (or common noun meaning 'mountain') in the genitive case (-i ending) after the oath particle wāw. The definite article ال is assimilated to the following ط (a solar letter), producing wal-ṭ-. The word ṭūr (طور) refers to a prominent mountain, specifically Mount Sinai in Quranic usage.
1.root: ط-و-ر (ṭ-w-r) — mountain, highland; in Quranic usage specifically Mount Sinai

1.meaning: And by a Book — oath by a divinely written scripture or record, continuing the series of oaths. The tanwīn indicates indefiniteness, suggesting a majestic or generic reference.
1.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case after the oath wāw. Kitāb (كتاب) is a verbal noun (maṣdar) from the root k-t-b meaning 'to write,' denoting a written record or scripture. The indefinite form with tanwīn gives it a quality of greatness or elevation.
1.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; كتاب = a book, a written record, scripture

2.meaning: Written — a passive participle describing the Book as inscribed, recorded. Refers to the divinely written scripture, emphasizing its fixed, recorded nature.
2.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول (mafʿūl) from the root s-ṭ-r, meaning 'to write in lines.' It functions as an adjective modifying kitāb (book) in the genitive case, agreeing in case and indefiniteness.
2.root: س-ط-ر (s-ṭ-r) — to write in lines, to inscribe; مسطور = that which has been written/inscribed

1.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
1.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
1.root: — (particle)

2.meaning: Parchment — fine skin or vellum used as writing material in ancient times; the medium on which the scripture is written.
2.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case, governed by the preposition fī ('in') in the preceding verse. Raqq (رَقّ) is a noun denoting thin fine parchment or skin used for writing — a classical writing material.
2.root: ر-ق-ق (r-q-q) — to be thin, fine; رَقّ = parchment, thin skin used for writing

3.meaning: Unrolled / spread open — a passive participle describing the parchment as laid open, unfurled, accessible for reading. Emphasizes the openness and completeness of the divine record.
3.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from the root n-sh-r meaning 'to spread out, to unfurl, to publish.' Adjective modifying raqq (parchment), agreeing in case and indefiniteness.
3.root: ن-ش-ر (n-sh-r) — to spread out, unfurl, publish; مَنْشُور = spread open, unrolled

1.meaning: By the House — oath by the Sacred House (the Kaʿbah in Mecca), the most sacred sanctuary in Islam.
1.grammar: Definite noun in the genitive case after the oath wāw. Al-Bayt (البيت) with the definite article is understood as a reference to the Sacred House (Kaʿbah) in Mecca, one of the most revered locations in Quranic oaths.
1.root: ب-ي-ت (b-y-t) — house, dwelling; البيت = the House, specifically the Kaʿbah

2.meaning: The frequented / much visited — describing the Sacred House as constantly visited, busy with worshippers. Some classical interpretations identify this as the Bayt al-Maʿmūr, the heavenly counterpart of the Kaʿbah.
2.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root ʿ-m-r meaning 'to inhabit, to frequent, to populate.' Adjective modifying al-bayt in the genitive case. Al-Maʿmūr can mean 'that which is populated/frequented.'
2.root: ع-م-ر (ʿ-m-r) — to inhabit, to frequent, to build up; مَعْمُور = frequented, inhabited, thriving

1.meaning: By the canopy / roof — oath by the elevated canopy or ceiling, referring to the sky or heavens as a raised roof over the earth.
1.grammar: Definite noun in the genitive case after the oath wāw. Al-Saqf (السقف) literally means a roof or ceiling; here it refers to the sky/heavens conceived as a raised canopy over the earth.
1.root: س-ق-ف (s-q-f) — to roof over; سَقْف = roof, ceiling, canopy

2.meaning: Raised high — an adjective describing the roof/sky as elevated, lifted high. Emphasizes the majestic height of the heavens.
2.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root r-f-ʿ meaning 'to raise, to lift.' Adjective modifying al-saqf (the roof) in the genitive case, describing the sky as raised high above the earth.
2.root: ر-ف-ع (r-f-ʿ) — to raise, to lift up; مَرْفُوع = raised, elevated

1.meaning: 'And the sea' — 'baḥr' is the sea or any large body of water; by extension a vast expanse. Made definite as 'the sea'.
1.grammar: A definite noun with the '-i' ending, which marks the genitive case — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). Prefixed 'wa' means 'and'.
1.root: ب-ح-ر (b-ḥ-r) — sea, vast body of water

2.meaning: Filled / kindled / overflowing — describing the sea as filled (with fire on the Day of Judgment, or referring to its present fullness). Classical commentators differ between 'set ablaze' and 'made to overflow.'
2.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root s-j-r meaning 'to kindle, to fill, to overflow.' Adjective modifying al-baḥr (the sea) in the genitive case.
2.root: س-ج-ر (s-j-r) — to kindle, to heat up, to fill; مَسْجُور = filled, kindled, set ablaze

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
2.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
2.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: Surely occurring / will certainly happen — emphasizing with certainty that the punishment of your Lord will inevitably come to pass.
4.grammar: The lām is lām al-tawkīd (emphatic lām), strengthening the affirmation. Wāqiʿ (وَاقِع) is an active participle (ism fāʿil) on the pattern فَاعِل from root w-q-ʿ (to fall upon, to occur, to happen). Indefinite nominative, predicate of inna: 'Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is surely occurring/coming.'
4.root: و-ق-ع (w-q-ʿ) — to fall, to occur; وَاقِع = that which is occurring, happening, befalling

1.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
1.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.
1.root: — (particle; no root)

2.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
2.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition)

4.meaning: A preventer / averter — one who repels or wards off. The punishment of the Lord has no preventer; nothing can hold it back.
4.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) on the pattern فَاعِل from root d-f-ʿ meaning 'to push away, to repel, to ward off.' Indefinite noun in the genitive case, used in a negation context: mā lahu min dāfiʿin — 'there is no preventer for it.'
4.root: د-ف-ع (d-f-ʿ) — to push away, to repel, to prevent; دَافِع = one who repels/prevents

1.meaning: Day — a span of time; frequently used to denote a momentous appointed Day, especially the Day of Resurrection and Judgment.
1.grammar: A noun ending in the accusative vowel -a. On a time-word like this the accusative commonly works adverbially to mean 'on the day (when…)' or 'on a day', setting the time-frame for an action.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, time

2.meaning: 'It heaves / sways / shakes in waves.' The verb describes a surging, rolling, convulsive motion — ground or matter trembling and undulating back and forth.

parts.en: to sway, heave, move in waves

2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the indicative. The 'ta-' prefix here marks a third-person feminine singular subject ('she / it'), commonly used for grammatically feminine nouns. The final '-u' is the indicative ending, signalling a plain ongoing or future statement ('it heaves / will heave').
2.root: م-و-ر (m-w-r) — to move to and fro, surge, sway

3.meaning: The sky / the heaven — the canopy overhead, the firmament; whatever rises above and overarches. The root sense is height and that which is elevated above.
3.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefixed al- ('the'). The -u ending signals the nominative case — the form typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing or undergoing the action). The word is grammatically feminine.
3.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness, that which is elevated

4.meaning: A violent shaking / trembling — describing the convulsive motion of the sky on the Day of Judgment, shaking violently.
4.grammar: Indefinite noun in the accusative case functioning as an adverbial of manner (mafʿūl muṭlaq or ḥāl), describing the manner of the sky's motion. Mawr (مَوْر) denotes rapid, violent oscillating movement.
4.root: م-و-ر (m-w-r) — to move rapidly, to surge, to oscillate violently; مَوْر = violent shaking

1.meaning: And will move away / march / travel — the mountains will be set in motion, drifting away as if they were mere clouds on the Last Day.

parts.en: will move / travel / march (3rd fem. singular imperfect)

1.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), third person feminine singular from root s-y-r meaning 'to travel, to walk, to move along.' The subject is al-jibāl (the mountains), which is feminine. Indicative mood (marfūʿ) marked by the final ḍamma.
1.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, to walk, to move; تَسِير = she/it travels, will travel

2.meaning: The mountains — the great, firmly rooted masses of rock and earth, often evoked as images of immovable solidity.
2.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'mountains', made definite by al- ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject or doer — the one the sentence is about.
2.root: ج-ب-ل (j-b-l) — mountain, that which is firmly fixed

3.meaning: A movement / marching — an indefinite noun describing the manner in which the mountains will move, emphasizing the completeness and gravity of the motion.
3.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) in the indefinite accusative, functioning as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) or adverbial of manner after tasīru (will move). Sayr is the maṣdar of sāra / yasīru.
3.root: س-ي-ر (s-y-r) — to travel, to move; سَيْر = the act of traveling/movement

1.meaning: 'So woe …' — a connective 'so/then' plus 'woe': an exclamation of impending doom, ruin, or grievous distress called down upon someone. It is a cry of warning and lament, not a literal noun of place.
1.grammar: The connective fa- ('so / then') prefixed to the noun 'woe.' The noun stands in the nominative with indefinite marking (the -un ending, tanwīn). Used this way it functions as an exclamation — 'woe (be) to …' — typically followed by 'to/for' someone.
1.root: و-ي-ل (w-y-l) — woe; ruin, doom, grievous distress

2.meaning: On that Day / that very Day — a temporal marker pointing to the Day of Judgment as the time when the promised punishment will descend.
2.grammar: A compound temporal expression: yawma (day, in the temporal accusative/ẓarf al-zamān) + ʾidh (when, at the time of) + tanwīn kasra (-in), forming the indeclinable yawmaʾidhin — 'on that day.' The tanwīn on ʾidh is a compensatory tanwīn replacing a following deleted clause.
2.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — يَوْم = day; يَوْمَئِذٍ = on that day (compound temporal)

3.meaning: To the deniers / beliers — those who persistently deny the truth; woe is proclaimed against them.

parts.en: accusative/genitive ending of sound masculine plural

3.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) of the Form II verb kadhdhaba (to deny, to call a liar), in the definite sound masculine plural, genitive case after the preposition li-. The Form II intensifies the action: mukadhdhibūn = persistent, deliberate deniers.
3.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, to deny; كَذَّبَ = to persistently deny; مُكَذِّب = one who denies

1.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
1.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

2.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
2.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: Vain discourse / idle talk / plunging into falsehood — engaging in frivolous argument, speculation, or immersion in falsehood.

parts.en: plunging into / wading through / vain discourse

4.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) from root kh-w-ḍ meaning 'to plunge into, to wade through (water), to engage in idle talk.' Here in the genitive case within the construction fī khawḍin (in vain discourse/idle plunging).
4.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to plunge into, to wade; خَوْض = plunging, wading, idle discourse

5.meaning: They play / amuse themselves — they are engaged in sport, diversion, or idle play, treating something lightly rather than seriously.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they …'). The 'ya-' prefix marks third-person present action and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing or habitual action. (The doubled initial 'y' reflects assimilation with a preceding word.)
5.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play, sport, amuse oneself

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: They will be thrust / pushed violently — on the Day of Judgment the deniers will be shoved forcefully into the Fire.
2.grammar: Passive imperfect (muḍāriʿ majhūl) of the Form II verb daʿʿa, third person masculine plural. Form II of d-ʿ-ʿ intensifies the action: to push/thrust violently and repeatedly. The passive indicates they are the recipients of this violent thrusting.
2.root: د-ع-ع (d-ʿ-ʿ) — to push, to thrust; دَعَّ = to shove violently; يُدَعُّون = they are thrust

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
3.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

4.meaning: Fire — blaze, flame; the burning element, and by extension the Fire of punishment.
4.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -i (genitive) ending typically marks the word as following a preposition (e.g. 'in / from the fire') or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the fire').
4.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — blazing, giving off light and heat; the source of fire and flame

5.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
5.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
5.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

6.meaning: A violent thrusting / shoving — the manner of being pushed into the Fire, emphasizing the forceful, harsh nature of the punishment.
6.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) of daʿʿa in the indefinite accusative, functioning as an absolute object (mafʿūl muṭlaq) emphasizing the manner or intensity of the action of thrusting.
6.root: د-ع-ع (d-ʿ-ʿ) — to push, thrust violently; دَعّ = a violent push/thrust

1.meaning: This (feminine) — a pointing word ('this one here') used for a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
1.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand. It is fixed in form and does not change for case; it commonly precedes the noun it points to.

2.meaning: The Fire — a definite noun for fire; frequently the term for the blazing punishment of the Hereafter (Hell).
2.grammar: Definite noun: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the following 'n', heard as 'an-nār'). The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically marking the subject of a sentence or the doer of an action.
2.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — fire, blaze

3.meaning: A feminine singular relative pronoun: 'the one which / that which / who' (referring to a single feminine thing). It introduces a descriptive clause that tells us more about a preceding feminine noun.
3.grammar: A relative pronoun, feminine singular, fixed in form (it does not change for case). It links a feminine noun to a following clause describing it, the equivalent of English 'which,' 'that,' or 'who.'

4.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
4.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

5.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
5.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.
5.root: — (preposition with pronoun)

6.meaning: You (a group) deny, reject as false, or treat as a lie — to actively brand something or someone untrue rather than merely doubting.

parts.en: you treat as a lie / deny

6.grammar: A present-tense Form II verb (the doubled, intensive pattern), giving the sense of firmly charging something with falsehood. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending adds plurality, so the 't-' prefix with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb stands in its plain, unaltered present state.
6.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, be false; to deny, call a lie

1.meaning: Is this then magic? — a rhetorical question challenging the deniers: do they dismiss the Quran as mere sorcery even when they clearly see the signs?
1.grammar: The hamza (اَ) is the interrogative particle and fa (فَ) is a connective conjunctive ('then, so'). Siḥr is an indefinite noun in the nominative case, functioning as the predicate of the nominal sentence: 'Is this then [merely] magic?'
1.root: س-ح-ر (s-ḥ-r) — to bewitch, to enchant; سِحْر = magic, sorcery

2.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
2.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

3.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
3.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

4.meaning: You — the standalone pronoun for a group of people ('you all', masculine or mixed). It is used for emphasis or as the subject standing on its own.
4.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'you all' (second-person masculine/mixed plural). Unlike pronoun endings attached to verbs or nouns, this word stands alone — typically to emphasize the subject or to begin an equational sentence ('you [are]…'). Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: You (a group) see, perceive with the eyes, or look and discern — to take in something visually or grasp it with sight and insight. (The bare verb form means 'you see'; any negation comes from a separate particle.)
6.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb meaning 'to see/perceive'. The stem alone is 2nd-person singular; the '-ūna' ending supplies plurality, so the 't-' prefix together with that ending marks 'you all' (second person masculine plural) acting now or habitually. The '-ūna' (not '-ū') shows the verb is in its plain, unaltered present state.
6.root: ب-ص-ر (b-ṣ-r) — sight, vision, to see and perceive

1.meaning: Burn in it / enter and roast in it: a command to a group to plunge into a blazing fire and undergo its scorching heat.
1.grammar: A masculine-plural command (imperative) of a defective (final-weak) verb, with a feminine 'it' attached as object. The weak final letter of the stem drops out and the wāw (-aw) marks the plural addressees ('you all burn'); -hā ('it') refers to the thing entered.
1.root: ص-ل-ي (ṣ-l-y) — roasting/burning in fire

2.meaning: An imperative addressed to a group: 'be patient, endure steadfastly, hold firm.' The root denotes restraining the self in the face of hardship, persevering without complaint. The opening particle attaches a sense of 'so' or 'then,' linking the command to something that precedes it.
2.grammar: A command verb addressed to a plural masculine 'you.' The -ū ending marks the plural addressee ('all of you, do this'). The prefixed fa- is a connective particle meaning roughly 'so' or 'then,' tying the directive to a preceding statement or condition.
2.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — patience, steadfast endurance

3.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
3.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: "You are patient / you endure steadfastly" — the act of a group exercising patience: self-restraint, perseverance, and steadfast endurance in the face of hardship.
5.grammar: A present/jussive verb. The ta-…-ū pattern marks a masculine plural addressee, 'you all'. The dropped final -na (taṣbirū rather than taṣbirūna) signals the jussive or subjunctive mood, typical after conditional particles ('if you are patient …').
5.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — patience, endurance, steadfastness

6.meaning: 'Equal / the same / all alike' — a noun-adjective expressing that two or more things make no difference and are on a par. It often appears in the sense 'it is all the same (whether… or…)'.
6.grammar: A singular indefinite noun used to mean 'equal/the same'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a/an…') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject or for the predicate that describes what something is.
6.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, equal, level

7.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
7.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

8.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
8.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

9.meaning: 'You are recompensed / repaid' — a passive verb meaning a group is given back what their deeds deserve, whether reward or penalty. The doer (the One who repays) is understood, not named.
9.grammar: A present/imperfect passive verb (form I). The tu- prefix with passive vowelling plus the -una ending marks a second-person masculine plural subject being acted upon ('you [all] are repaid'). The -una (not -u) shows the indicative mood, used for plain factual statements.
9.root: ج-ز-ى (j-z-y) — recompense, requital, repaying in kind

10.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
10.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

11.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
11.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

12.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

2.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.
2.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself)

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
3.root: — (particle)

4.meaning: 'Gardens' — the plural of a lush, walled garden thick with trees whose foliage covers the ground. The root sense is concealment by dense greenery; it is the standard word for the gardens of Paradise.
4.grammar: An indefinite sound feminine plural noun ('gardens'). The '-in' (tanwīn) ending marks it as indefinite ('some gardens'), and for this plural form it stands in the oblique case (genitive or accusative), used after prepositions/possessives or as a direct object.
4.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide (hence a dense garden)

5.meaning: And pleasure / bliss / delight — one of the blessings of Paradise, paired with fruits: a life of enjoyment and delight.
5.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case, coordinated with fākiha (fruit) by the conjunction wāw. Naʿīm (نَعِيم) is an intensive form denoting abundant, overflowing pleasantness and comfort — the bliss of Paradise.
5.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — to be pleasant, comfortable; نَعِيم = bliss, comfort, abundant pleasure

1.meaning: Ones enjoying themselves, taking delight and ease — people relishing comfort, amusement, and the good things they have.
1.grammar: A doer-noun ('ones taking delight') in the masculine plural. The -īna ending is the masculine plural in its object/oblique form — the shape the plural takes when the word is a direct object, follows a preposition, or describes such a noun. It often functions to describe the state someone is in ('delighting, at their ease').
1.root: ف-ك-ه (f-k-h) — to enjoy, take delight; fruit, pleasantry

2.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
2.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
2.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

3.meaning: He gave them, He granted them — a past act of one party bestowing or bringing something to a group; joined with 'them'.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb from Form IV (to give or bring) with an attached object pronoun. The verb itself is third-person masculine singular, 'he …'. The attached -hum means 'them' (a masculine group), marking the recipients of the giving. The verb's own ending is a long -ā that stays fixed and does not change for case or mood.
3.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, bring; (Form IV) to give, bestow

4.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
4.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

5.meaning: 'And He guarded / shielded them' — to protect, ward off harm from, and keep safe.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb (a defective verb ending in a weak letter, here appearing as the long 'ā') with an attached object pronoun. The suffix -hum is the object, 'them' (a group of males or mixed group). The bare past-tense form with no subject suffix indicates the doer is 'he'.
5.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, to shield, to protect (the root of taqwā)

6.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
6.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
6.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

7.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.

8.meaning: The blazing Fire; a fiercely flaming, intensely hot fire — a name for the Hellfire.
8.grammar: A definite noun: the prefix al- means 'the'. The stem is on the faʿīl pattern conveying intensity (a fiercely kindled fire). The final -i is the genitive ending, typically appearing after a preposition or linking it to a preceding noun in an 'of' relationship.
8.root: ج-ح-م (j-ḥ-m) — to blaze, burn fiercely; intensely kindled fire

1.meaning: 'Eat!' — a command addressed to more than one person, telling a group to eat or partake of food.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending directs the command at a group ('you all, eat!'). This verb's command form drops its original first root letter, so the stem appears simply as kul-. The silent alif written after the wāw is a spelling convention for the plural ending.
1.root: ا-ك-ل ('-k-l) — eating, consuming food

2.meaning: 'And drink!' — a command addressed to a group to drink, joined to what precedes by 'and'.
2.grammar: A command (imperative) verb with a connecting 'wa' ('and') prefixed. The -ū ending directs the order at a plural 'you' (a group of males or a mixed group): 'and you all, drink!' The initial vowel of the stem is a helping vowel that drops after the prefix.
2.root: ش-ر-ب (sh-r-b) — drinking

3.meaning: In complete satisfaction / with wholesome enjoyment — the believers will eat and drink in Paradise in a state of complete well-being and satisfaction, without harm or regret.
3.grammar: An adjective or adverbial in the indefinite accusative, functioning as a ḥāl (circumstantial complement) or as a special predicate meaning 'wholesomely' or 'in enjoyment.' Hanīʾ (هَنِيء) means pleasant, wholesome, without ill effect — the opposite of food that causes regret or harm.
3.root: ه-ن-أ (h-n-ʾ) — to be pleasant, wholesome, without harm; هَنِيء = pleasant, satisfying

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
4.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
4.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

5.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
5.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

6.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
6.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: Reclining / leaning back — resting at ease while propped against a support, the posture of comfort and repose.
1.grammar: An active participle (a describing word) of the form meaning 'ones who recline/lean back.' The mu- prefix marks it as such a doer-word; the third radical of the root is a hamza (a glottal stop), seen in the stem. The -īna ending is the masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used here as the plural of those described and matching that case.
1.root: و-ك-ء (w-k-ʾ) — to lean, recline, prop oneself up

2.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
2.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

3.meaning: Couches or thrones — raised, cushioned seats or beds of honor on which one reclines in comfort and dignity. The plural denotes a set of such seats.
3.grammar: Plural noun, indefinite. The final -in (genitive with nunation) marks an unspecified 'some couches'; the genitive case typically appears after a preposition or in an 'of'-type linkage to another noun.
3.root: س-ر-ر (s-r-r) — joy, gladness (a couch being associated with delight and ease)

4.meaning: Arranged in rows / lined up — describing the cushions or couches in Paradise as set out in orderly rows, conveying abundance and splendid arrangement.

parts.en: arranged in rows / lined up (passive participle, feminine)

4.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) feminine form from root ṣ-f-f meaning 'to arrange in a row, to line up.' The feminine form agrees with its noun (cushions/couches, which is feminine). Indefinite genitive after a preceding preposition.
4.root: ص-ف-ف (ṣ-f-f) — to arrange in a row; مَصْفُوفة = arranged in rows, lined up

5.meaning: 'And We joined them in marriage / paired them' — to give in marriage, or more broadly to couple and pair people together.
5.grammar: Past-tense verb with attached pronouns. The intensified 'zawwaja' pattern means to actively pair or wed. The suffix -nā is the doer, 'we'; the suffix -hum is the object, 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group). The -nā ending specifically marks a completed action done by 'we'.
5.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, spouse, to couple together

6.meaning: 'With / to ḥūr' — fair companions of Paradise, described as having strikingly white, lustrous eyes set off against deep black; pure, beautiful mates.
6.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition 'bi' ('with/by/to'). The ending -in is indefinite and genitive — the genitive case is required here because the word follows a preposition; the final -n marks it as indefinite. 'Ḥūr' is a plural denoting an intense contrast of white and black in the eye.
6.root: ح-و-ر (ḥ-w-r) — whiteness contrasted with deep black (of the eye)

7.meaning: 'Wide-eyed, with large beautiful eyes' — having big, lustrous eyes, a mark of beauty.
7.grammar: A plural adjective (singular 'ʿaynāʾ', meaning a woman with large lovely eyes). The ending -in is indefinite and genitive, agreeing with a preceding genitive noun it describes; the final -n marks indefiniteness.
7.root: ع-ي-ن (ʿ-y-n) — eye; largeness/beauty of the eye

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.
1.root: — (relative pronoun)

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: And followed them — their offspring followed them in faith, so God joins them together in Paradise as a mercy.
3.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), third person feminine singular from root t-b-ʿ in Form VIII (ittabaʿa = to follow, to come after). The feminine form agrees with the subject dhurriyyatuhum (their offspring) which is being discussed. The object suffix -hum refers to the believing men/parents.
3.root: ت-ب-ع (t-b-ʿ) — to follow, to come after; اتَّبَعَ = to follow closely; اتَّبَعَت = she/it followed

4.meaning: Their offspring / descendants — their progeny who followed them in faith; God will unite them with their parents in Paradise.
4.grammar: Noun in the nominative case (subject of ittabaʿat), with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum. Dhurriyya (ذُرِّيَّة) is a collective noun denoting descendants/offspring — it is feminine in form, hence the feminine verb ittabaʿat.
4.root: ذ-ر-ر (dh-r-r) or ذ-ر-ي (dh-r-y) — to scatter seed, to beget; ذُرِّيَّة = offspring, progeny

5.meaning: In / with faith — the offspring followed their parents in faith (īmān), thus qualifying for the reward of reunion in Paradise.
5.grammar: Prepositional phrase: bi-īmānin, 'with/in faith.' The preposition bi introduces the genitive indefinite noun īmān, which is the verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form IV āmana (to believe). The tanwīn marks indefiniteness.
5.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to believe; إِيمَان = faith, belief (maṣdar of Form IV)

6.meaning: We will join / unite them — God will join the offspring with their parents in Paradise, as an act of divine grace and mercy.

parts.en: We joined / united / attached (1st plural perfect, Form IV)

6.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), first person plural from root l-ḥ-q in Form IV (alḥaqa = to attach, to join, to append). The wāw of the first person plural is contracted into the nā suffix. Subject is Allah (implied first person plural of majesty).
6.root: ل-ح-ق (l-ḥ-q) — to reach, to catch up, to join; أَلْحَقَ = to attach, to join, to unite (Form IV)

7.meaning: An expression meaning 'at them' or 'with them' — the preposition 'bi' (with, by, at) joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group). The exact shade ('at/by/with them') depends on the verb it accompanies.
7.grammar: A preposition (bi-, 'with/by/at') with the attached pronoun -him ('them,' for a group of males). The pronoun is in the genitive, the case always required after a preposition.

8.meaning: Their offspring / descendants — progeny, children, and the generations springing from someone, with an attached pronoun 'their.'
8.grammar: A noun with the accusative ending '-a', which typically marks it as the direct object of a verb. The attached '-hum' is a third-person masculine plural possessive pronoun ('their'), showing ownership.
8.root: ذ-ر-و/ي (dh-r-w / dh-r-y) — to scatter, spread, propagate (offspring)

9.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
9.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

10.meaning: We will not deprive them / We will not diminish them — God will not reduce the reward of the parents due to the elevation of their offspring; both are fully rewarded.
10.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), first person plural from root ʾ-l-t meaning 'to diminish, to reduce, to deprive of.' With the object suffix -hum. In context it is preceded by the negation mā: 'We did not deprive them [of any of their deeds].'
10.root: أ-ل-ت (ʾ-l-t) — to diminish, to reduce, to deprive; أَلَتَ = he diminished; أَلَتْنَاهُمْ = we deprived them

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: Their deeds / their work — each person is bound by what they themselves have earned; no one bears another's burden.

parts.en: their (3rd masculine plural possessive suffix, genitive)

12.grammar: Noun in the genitive case (after preposition bi-: bi-mā kasabū 'by what they earned'), with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -him. ʿAmal (عَمَل) is a common noun meaning deed, work, action.
12.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, to act; عَمَل = deed, action, work

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

14.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
14.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
14.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'all, every, each, the whole of.' It expresses totality — when joined to a following noun it means 'every (one)' or 'the entirety of' that thing.
15.grammar: A noun of totality with the final -u ending (nominative). The -u typically marks it as the subject or the thing being spoken about. It normally attaches to a following noun to mean 'every / all of' it.

16.meaning: Every person / each individual — every soul is pledged to what it has earned; there is individual accountability.

parts.en: a person / an individual / a man

16.grammar: The word imruʾ (امرؤ) is an unusual noun with a variable initial vowel (imruʾ/marʾ). Here in the genitive case (imriʾin) after the particle kull: kullu imriʾin (every person). It is a noun referring to a person or individual, masculine.
16.root: م-ر-أ (m-r-ʾ) — امرؤ / مَرْء = a person, a man, an individual

17.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
17.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

18.meaning: He earned / acquired — to gain, accumulate, or bring upon oneself something through one's own action or effort (good deeds or sins, gain or its consequences), presented as completed.
18.grammar: Past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The bare '-a' ending is the basic past form with no added suffix, presenting the earning as an accomplished act.

19.meaning: Is pledged / is held hostage — each soul is held as a pledge against what it has earned; accountable and bound to its own deeds.

parts.en: pledged / held as security / in pawn

19.grammar: An intensive adjective (or passive participle) on the pattern فَعِيل from root r-h-n meaning 'to pledge, to give as security, to pawn.' Functions as the predicate of the nominal sentence: kullu imriʾin bimā kasaba rahīnun — 'every person is pledged by what he earned.'
19.root: ر-ه-ن (r-h-n) — to pledge, to pawn, to give as security; رَهِين = pledged, in pawn, held accountable

1.meaning: And We will provide them / And We supplied them — God grants the People of Paradise additional provisions: fruit, meat, and whatever they desire.

parts.en: We provided / supplied / extended (1st plural perfect, Form IV)

1.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), first person plural from root m-d-d in Form IV (amdada = to extend, to supply, to provide). With the object suffix -hum. Amdada carries the sense of supplying in abundance, extending generously.
1.root: م-د-د (m-d-d) — to extend, to stretch; أَمَدَّ = to supply abundantly, to provide (Form IV)

2.meaning: With fruit — the people of Paradise are served with fruit, one of the many delights and provisions of the Garden.
2.grammar: Prepositional phrase: bi + indefinite genitive noun. Fākiha (فَاكِهَة) is a collective noun meaning fruit(s) — the delicious produce of Paradise. The tanwīn marks indefiniteness, suggesting abundance and variety.
2.root: ف-ك-ه (f-k-h) — to be merry, to enjoy; فَاكِهَة = fruit (that which gives enjoyment)

3.meaning: And meat — among the provisions of Paradise is meat of whatever the believers desire.
3.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case, coordinated with fākiha (fruit) and other provisions by the conjunction wāw. Laḥm (لَحْم) means meat, flesh — one of the foods granted to the people of Paradise.
3.root: ل-ح-م (l-ḥ-m) — to join closely; لَحْم = meat, flesh

4.meaning: A fused word combining the preposition 'min' ('from', 'of', 'about') with the relative/indefinite 'mā' ('what', 'that which'). Together: 'from what', 'about that which', 'of what'.
4.grammar: The preposition 'min' and the word 'mā' merge in pronunciation (the 'n' assimilating into the 'm'). 'min' governs a genitive, and 'mā' here functions as a relative pronoun introducing a clause ('that which …'). These are indeclinable particles without case endings.

5.meaning: They crave or have an appetite for — to desire eagerly, to long for something pleasurable, especially food.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb (form VIII), third-person masculine plural. The ya-...-ūna frame means 'they (men) desire'; the final -ūna marks the plain indicative ('do / are doing').
5.root: ش-ه-و (sh-h-w) — desire, appetite, craving

1.meaning: To quarrel, dispute, or wrangle with one another — a reciprocal contending in which parties pull against each other, in the form 'they contend among themselves.'
1.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reciprocal pattern (Form VI), which adds the sense of 'doing something to one another.' The 'ya-' prefix marks the third-person masculine (its bare form is third-person masculine singular); the plural 'they' is supplied by the '-ūna' ending, which also signals the indicative mood (a plain statement, 'they dispute'), as opposed to a shortened subjunctive/jussive form.
1.root: ن-ز-ع (n-z-ʿ) — to pull out, snatch, contend

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: A cup / a goblet — the people of Paradise pass around cups of pure, pleasant drink.
3.grammar: Indefinite noun in the accusative case, functioning as the object of yatanāzaʿūna (they pass around). Kaʾs (كَأْس) is a drinking cup or goblet; in Quranic usage it often refers to a cup of wine or pure drink in Paradise.
3.root: ك-أ-س (k-ʾ-s) — كَأْس = a cup, drinking vessel, goblet

4.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
4.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

5.meaning: Idle / vain talk / frivolous speech — the drink in Paradise produces no idle or offensive talk among its drinkers.

parts.en: idle talk / vain speech / frivolous words

5.grammar: Indefinite noun in the nominative case, functioning as the subject of lā laghwun fīhā — 'there is no idle talk in it.' Laghw (لَغْو) denotes futile, worthless, frivolous speech or action.
5.root: ل-غ-و (l-gh-w) — to be idle, futile; لَغْو = idle/vain talk, futility

6.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
6.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
6.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

7.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
7.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

8.meaning: Sin / sinful speech / incitement to sin — the drink of Paradise is free from both idle talk and sinful incitement.

parts.en: sin / sinful speech / incitement to sin

8.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form II of ʾ-th-m meaning 'to charge with sin, to lead to sin.' Indefinite nominative, subject of the negation: wa-lā taʾthīmun — 'and no sinful talk.' The Form II maṣdar denotes the act of accusing of sin or of saying sinful things.
8.root: أ-ث-م (ʾ-th-m) — to sin, to be sinful; تَأْثِيم = sinful speech, incitement to sin (Form II maṣdar)

1.meaning: And there will circulate around them / will go around serving them — youths will circulate among the people of Paradise to serve them.

parts.en: will circulate / will go around (3rd masculine singular imperfect)

1.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), third person masculine singular from root ṭ-w-f meaning 'to go around, to circumambulate, to circulate.' Indicative mood marked by the final ḍamma. Subject is ghilmānun (youths) which follows.
1.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, to circulate; يَطُوف = he goes around/circulates

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
2.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
2.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Boys / youths — the young servants of Paradise who circulate among the blessed to serve them.
3.grammar: Indefinite noun in the nominative case, subject of yaṭūfu (circulates). Ghilmān (غِلْمَان) is the broken plural of ghulām (غُلَام), meaning a young boy, youth, or servant. Indefinite nominative with tanwīn.
3.root: غ-ل-م (gh-l-m) — to be youthful; غُلَام = a youth, young boy; غِلْمَان = youths (plural)

4.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
4.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

5.meaning: As though they / as if they (were) — the comparison particle 'ka-anna' ('as if', likening one thing to another) joined to the pronoun 'they', introducing a supposed or apparent state.
5.grammar: A compound particle: 'ka-' ('like/as') fused with the emphatic 'anna' ('that') to form 'ka-anna' = 'as if'. It governs the following pronoun '-hum' ('they'), which takes the accusative form as its subject. It sets up a comparison: things appear as though a certain (often untrue) state held.
5.root: — (particles; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: Pearls — the youths of Paradise are compared to well-preserved pearls in their purity, beauty, and lustrous appearance.
6.grammar: Indefinite noun in the nominative case, predicate of the comparison (they are like pearls). Luʾluʾ (لُؤْلُؤ) is a noun meaning pearls — beautiful, lustrous, and carefully preserved gems. The word has a reduplicated sound giving it an evocative quality.
6.root: ل-أ-ل-أ (l-ʾ-l-ʾ) — to shimmer, to gleam; لُؤْلُؤ = pearl

7.meaning: Well-protected / carefully preserved / hidden away — describing the pearls (and the youths or maidens) as being kept safe and pure, untouched.
7.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root k-n-n meaning 'to conceal, to protect, to preserve carefully.' Indefinite nominative, adjective modifying luʾluʾ (pearls) — pearls that are kept safely hidden and pristine.
7.root: ك-ن-ن (k-n-n) — to hide, to protect; مَكْنُون = well-protected, hidden, carefully preserved

1.meaning: And will approach / and turn to one another — they will approach each other, asking questions among themselves about their worldly lives.

parts.en: approached / turned toward (3rd masculine singular perfect, Form IV)

1.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), third person masculine singular from root q-b-l in Form IV (aqbala = to come forward, to approach, to turn to face). The subject is the people of Paradise, turning toward one another in conversation.
1.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to face, to come before; أَقْبَلَ = to approach, to turn toward (Form IV)

2.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
2.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
2.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

3.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
3.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

4.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
4.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
4.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

5.meaning: They ask one another / inquiring among themselves — the people of Paradise turn to each other and question one another about their past lives.

parts.en: they question one another / ask each other (3rd masculine plural imperfect, Form VI)
accusative ending (dropped final nūn — actually kept here)

5.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), third person masculine plural from root s-ʾ-l in Form VI (tasāʾala = to question one another mutually). Form VI expresses mutual or reciprocal action. The -ūna ending is in the indicative mood.
5.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask; تَسَاءَلَ = to ask each other (Form VI); يَتَسَاءَلُون = they question one another

1.meaning: 'They said' — a group uttered or stated something. Past-tense speech attributed to a plural subject.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (said)'. It states a completed act of speaking in the past.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

2.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
2.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

3.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
3.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
3.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

4.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
4.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: Our family / our people — the believers in Paradise long for their loved ones to join them, calling out that they used to supplicate for them.
6.grammar: Noun in the genitive case (after fī: fī ahl = among family) with the first-person plural possessive suffix -nā. Ahl (أَهْل) means family, household, people — those who belong together.
6.root: أ-ه-ل (ʾ-h-l) — أَهْل = family, people, household

7.meaning: Apprehensive, fearful, anxious — filled with a wary dread, dreading some harm or outcome.
7.grammar: A masculine plural active participle (form IV) describing those who possess a quality — 'ones who are apprehensive.' The -īna ending is the masculine sound plural in the accusative/genitive case (used for objects, after prepositions, or as a descriptive state).
7.root: ش-ف-ق (sh-f-q) — to be apprehensive, fearful, tenderly anxious

1.meaning: 'He bestowed a favor, showed grace, conferred a benefit' — to give generously out of kindness. It can also mean to remind someone of a favor done, depending on usage.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he conferred a favor.' The doubled final letter (shadda) reflects the root's last two identical consonants. The 'fa' prefix connects it to what precedes ('so/then').
1.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to bestow favor, show grace; also to remind of a benefit

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: 'Upon us' / 'over us' / 'against us' — the preposition ʿalā ('on, over, upon') with an attached 'us'. It conveys something resting on, incumbent upon, or bearing against the group.
3.grammar: A preposition (ʿalā, 'upon/over') with an attached pronoun, first person plural (-nā, 'us'). When a pronoun is attached, ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay-. Such prepositional phrases put their pronoun in the object/genitive role.

4.meaning: And He protected us / and He shielded us — God warded off the punishment of the scorching wind (samūm) from the believers.

parts.en: He protected us / He shielded us (3rd singular perfect + 1st plural object)

4.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), third person masculine singular from root w-q-y meaning 'to protect, to guard, to shield.' With the first-person plural object suffix -nā. Waqā is a verb that can take a double object (protect X from Y).
4.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to protect, to guard; وَقَى = he protected; وَقَانَا = he protected us

5.meaning: Torment, punishment, or chastisement — severe, painful suffering imposed as a penalty.
5.grammar: A singular noun. The final -a (fatḥa) marks the accusative case, the form used for a direct object of a verb, or for the first noun of a possessive pair ('the punishment of …') when that whole phrase is itself an object.
5.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish

6.meaning: 'Scorching / intensely hot' — a piercing, burning heat; a hot blast or searing wind that penetrates.
6.grammar: A definite singular noun (with the assimilated 'al-,' its sun-letter s doubling the following sound). The final -i is the genitive ending — the case used when the word is linked to a preceding noun ('… of scorching heat') or follows a preposition.
6.root: س-م-م (s-m-m) — piercing heat; that which penetrates pores

1.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
1.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

2.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
2.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

3.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
3.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
3.root: — (preposition)

4.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
4.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

5.meaning: We used to call / invoke / supplicate Him — in their gratitude in Paradise, the believers recall that they used to call upon God in the world.

parts.en: we call / invoke / supplicate (1st plural imperfect)

5.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), first person plural from root d-ʿ-w meaning 'to call, to invoke, to supplicate.' With the third-person masculine singular object suffix -hu (referring to God). Used with the past auxiliary kunnā (we used to be) to form the past continuous.
5.root: د-ع-و (d-ʿ-w) — to call, to invoke, to supplicate; نَدْعُو = we call/invoke

6.meaning: An emphasis particle fused with a pronoun, meaning 'indeed He' or 'truly He'. The particle inna strongly affirms and certifies the statement that follows ('it is certainly the case that…'), with 'He' as its subject.
6.grammar: The emphasising particle inna ('indeed/truly') with the attached pronoun -hu ('He'). inna affirms and strengthens the whole statement and grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its subject. The lengthened -hū is how this pronoun is pronounced after an -u vowel.

7.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
7.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

8.meaning: The Most Kind / the Benevolent / the Righteous — one of God's names, describing Him as the source of all goodness and righteousness.

parts.en: the Most Kind / the Benevolent / the Righteous

8.grammar: Definite noun (used as a Divine Name) in the nominative case. Al-Barr (البَرّ) is one of the ninety-nine names of God, meaning the Most Good, Most Kind, Most Righteous — the source of all goodness and benefit.
8.root: ب-ر-ر (b-r-r) — to be good, righteous, kind; البَرّ = the Most Kind/Righteous (Divine Name)

9.meaning: The Most Merciful / Ever-Merciful (al-Raḥīm) — a name of Allah from the root of mercy, in a pattern denoting constant, enduring mercy that is actively bestowed.
9.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'r', said ar-raḥīm). A 'faʿīl' adjective-form denoting an enduring, established quality of mercy. The final -u is the nominative case ending, typically marking a subject, predicate, or descriptor of such.

1.meaning: So remind / therefore admonish — a command to the Prophet to continue giving reminders, for reminder benefits those who will receive it.

parts.en: remind / admonish (2nd masculine singular imperative, Form II)

1.grammar: Imperative verb (ṣīghat al-amr), second person masculine singular from root dh-k-r in Form II (dhakkara = to remind repeatedly, to admonish). Form II intensifies the base meaning of remembering — to actively cause remembrance. The final sukūn marks the imperative.
1.root: ذ-ك-ر (dh-k-r) — to remember; ذَكَّرَ = to remind (Form II); فَذَكِّرْ = so remind!

2.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
2.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

3.meaning: 'You' — the standalone, independent pronoun for addressing a single male person directly.
3.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, second-person masculine singular. Unlike attached pronoun suffixes, it stands alone and is typically used to identify or emphasize the subject ('you [yourself]').

4.meaning: By the grace / through the blessing — by the grace and blessing of God, the Prophet is not a soothsayer or madman.
4.grammar: Prepositional phrase: bi + niʿmati (in construct state, first term of iḍāfa). Niʿma (نِعْمَة) means a blessing, favor, or grace from God. In construct state (niʿmati), the tāʾ marbūṭa is pronounced as a regular tāʾ before the possessive suffix.
4.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — to be pleasant, to bless; نِعْمَة = blessing, grace, favor

5.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
5.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
5.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

6.meaning: A soothsayer / diviner — the disbelievers accused the Prophet of being a fortune-teller or diviner, dismissing his prophecies.

parts.en: with / by (preposition, marking predicate after denial)

6.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case after the preposition bi-, which serves as a predicate marker in Arabic after negations (mā anta bi-kāhinin = 'you are not a soothsayer'). Kāhin (كَاهِن) is an active participle of k-h-n meaning a diviner, soothsayer, or fortune-teller.
6.root: ك-ه-ن (k-h-n) — to divine, to foretell; كَاهِن = soothsayer, diviner

7.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

8.meaning: A madman / a possessed person — another accusation hurled at the Prophet by the disbelievers, dismissing his message as madness.
8.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root j-n-n meaning 'to be concealed, to be touched by jinn, to be mad.' Indefinite genitive, predicate after the negation construction (wa-lā majnūnin = 'nor a madman').
8.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to conceal, to possess (by jinn); مَجْنُون = possessed, insane, madman

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
1.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'They say / they keep saying' — a present-tense verb of speaking: to say, utter, or assert in words.
2.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'), from a hollow (middle-vowel) root. The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are saying.'
2.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — speech; saying, uttering, asserting

3.meaning: A poet — one who composes poetry; indefinite, 'a poet.'
