3.grammar: A noun (in form an active participle, 'one who composes poetry') with the -un ending: nominative case with nunation. The final -n marks it indefinite ('a poet'), and the -u base is the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is a poet').
3.root: ش-ع-ر (sh-ʿ-r) — to perceive, sense; poetry

4.meaning: We wait / we bide our time — the disbelievers claimed they were waiting for misfortune to befall the Prophet.

parts.en: we wait / we bide our time (1st plural imperfect, Form V)

4.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), first person plural from root r-b-ṣ in Form V (tarabbaṣa = to wait, to bide one's time, to watch and wait). Form V adds a reflexive/intensive nuance to the base meaning. Indicative mood.
4.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, to watch; تَرَبَّصَ = to bide one's time (Form V); نَتَرَبَّصُ = we wait

5.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

6.meaning: Doubt, suspicion, disquieting uncertainty — the kind of wavering that unsettles the heart, stronger than a passing question. It names the state of not being at rest about whether something is true.
6.grammar: A masculine singular noun shown with an -a ending and no tanwin. This is the accusative (mansub) noun governed by the negating particle la — its ism — taking a bare form to express absolute negation, conveying that the whole category is ruled out ('there is no doubt whatsoever').
6.root: ر-ي-ب (r-y-b) — doubt, disquiet

7.meaning: The misfortune of time / the blows of fate / death — what the disbelievers hoped would befall the Prophet: death or calamity as a stroke of fate.

parts.en: the misfortune of time / fate / death

7.grammar: Definite noun in the genitive case (after the preposition rīb or after 'stroke of'). Al-Manūn (المَنُون) is a poetic word for fate or death — the relentless turning of time that brings misfortune. Derived from m-n-n (to allot, to dole out).
7.root: م-ن-ن (m-n-n) — to dole out, to cut; المَنُون = fate, death, the misfortunes of time

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.
1.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak

2.meaning: Wait! — a command to the disbelievers: let them wait along with the believers; the outcome will be clear.

parts.en: Wait! / Bide your time! (2nd masculine plural imperative, Form V)

2.grammar: Imperative verb (ṣīghat al-amr), second person masculine plural from root r-b-ṣ in Form V (tarabbaṣa). The Form V imperative drops the ta- prefix and the final -ūna indicative ending becomes -ū. Addressed to the disbelievers.
2.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait; تَرَبَّصُوا = Wait! (plural imperative)

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'so indeed I…' — joining 'so/then' to an emphatic assertion about the speaker, strongly affirming what follows as true and certain.

4.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

5.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.

6.meaning: Those who wait / the waiters — the plural active participle of Form V of r-b-ṣ, referring to those who bide their time. The believers are also waiters — but for divine victory.

parts.en: those who wait / those who bide their time (Form V active participle, plural)
accusative/genitive ending of sound masculine plural

6.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) of Form V tarabbaṣa, in the definite sound masculine plural, genitive/accusative case (marked by -ūna/-īna). Refers to both the disbelievers and believers who are each waiting — for different outcomes.
6.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait; مُتَرَبِّص = one who waits; المُتَرَبِّصِين = those who wait

parts.en: commands / orders / instructs (3rd feminine singular imperfect)

2.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), third person feminine singular from root ʾ-m-r meaning 'to command, to order, to instruct.' The feminine form agrees with the subject aḥlāmuhum (their minds/dreams), which is the plural of ḥulm (dream/reason), and plural of non-human nouns takes feminine agreement.
2.root: أ-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, to order; تَأْمُر = it commands; تَأْمُرُهُمْ = it commands them

7.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.

parts.en: transgressors / those who overstep bounds (active participle, plural)
accusative/nominative marker of sound masculine plural

3.grammar: Perfect verb (māḍī), third person masculine singular from root q-w-l in Form V (taqawwala = to fabricate speech, to attribute speech falsely). Form V of q-w-l specifically means to invent or make up words and attribute them falsely. Object suffix -hu refers to the Quran.

1.meaning: Then let them bring / let them produce — a challenge to the disbelievers to bring a hadith (statement/discourse) like the Quran if they think it is fabricated.

1.grammar: The particle fa introduces the consequence. Lām al-amr (لِ) + jussive form: li-yaʾtū (let them bring/come). The verb is from root ʾ-t-y in Form I (to come, to bring), third person masculine plural, jussive mood (majzūm) — final wāw after dropping nūn.
1.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, to bring; يَأْتِي = he comes; فَلْيَأْتُوا = then let them bring

2.grammar: Prepositional phrase: bi + indefinite genitive noun. Ḥadīth (حَدِيث) means a statement, discourse, or narration — a piece of speech. Here the challenge is: produce a ḥadīth (statement/discourse) like it, if you are truthful.
2.root: ح-د-ث (ḥ-d-th) — to occur, to speak; حَدِيث = speech, discourse, narration

3.root: م-ث-ل (m-th-l) — to resemble; likeness, similitude, equivalent

4.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
4.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

5.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
5.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

6.meaning: The plural of 'ṣādiq': 'truthful ones', 'those who speak the truth', 'the sincere and reliable'. It describes people whose words and conduct match reality.
6.grammar: 'ṣādiq' is an active participle ('one who is truthful'). The '-īna' ending is a 'sound' masculine plural marker; the '-ī-' form (rather than '-ū-') signals that the noun is functioning as an object or is governed by a preposition/particle, while the '-na' completes the plural ('the truthful ones').
6.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness, sincerity, to speak truly

4.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'they listen, give ear, pay attention' — to direct one's hearing toward something attentively, seeking to take it in. The root is hearing and listening; this intensified form adds the sense of deliberately straining to hear.

2.root: — (particle with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

3.meaning: Daughters — the disbelievers attributed daughters to God (in their belief that angels were God's daughters), while they themselves preferred sons.
3.grammar: Definite noun in the nominative case. Al-Banāt (البَنَات) is the broken plural (or sound feminine plural) of ibn/bint, meaning daughters or girls. Used in the rhetorical argument against the polytheists who claimed angels were daughters of God.
3.root: ب-ن-و/ي (b-n-w/y) — to build, to beget; بِنْت = daughter; بَنَات = daughters

4.meaning: And for you / and to you / and yours — expressing that something belongs to, or is due to, a group of people.
4.grammar: A small phrase: 'and' + the preposition 'for/to' + the attached pronoun 'you' (masculine plural), giving 'and for you'. The pronoun normally ends -kum, but here shows -kumu, the vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with 'the' (al-).

5.meaning: Sons / boys — the disbelievers kept sons for themselves while attributing daughters to God; a critique of their double standard.

parts.en: accusative/genitive ending of sound masculine plural

5.grammar: Definite noun in the nominative/accusative case. Al-Banūn (البَنُون) is the sound masculine plural of ibn (son), using the -ūna/-īna plural pattern. The rhetorical question: a-lahum al-dhukūr wa-lahu al-ināth — 'are sons for them and daughters for Him?'
5.root: ب-ن-و/ي (b-n-w/y) — to build, to beget; اِبْن = son; بَنُون = sons (plural)

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
1.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: Means "you ask them" — the act of requesting or questioning, done in the present/ongoing sense by "you," directed at "them."
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ta- prefix marks a masculine singular "you" as the doer; the -u indicative ending signals a plain, ongoing statement; the attached -hum ("them") is the object being asked.
2.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, request, question

3.meaning: A reward, wage, or recompense — the return earned for work or conduct, whether worldly pay or otherworldly recompense.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'a reward.' The final '-an' (tanwīn fatḥa) marks the indefinite accusative case, the case used for the object of a verb (e.g. of 'to give'), giving the sense 'a reward.'
3.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense for what one does

4.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
4.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A debt / a ransom / a fine — do they ask you for a compensation or reward for delivering the message? The Prophet asks for no payment.
6.grammar: Indefinite noun in the genitive case (after the preposition min: min maghramin = for a debt/compensation). Maghram (مَغْرَم) can mean a debt, a penalty, or a burdensome payment — something that causes hardship.
6.root: غ-ر-م (gh-r-m) — to incur a debt, to be penalized; مَغْرَم = debt, penalty, burdensome payment

7.meaning: Overburdened / weighed down — by debt or the burden of payment. The question asks if the disbelievers are burdened by having to pay the Prophet.
7.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) of Form IV athqala (to weigh down, to overburden), in the sound masculine plural nominative with the predicate ending. Muthqalūn = those who have been weighed down, overburdened (by debt or obligation).
7.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — to be heavy; أَثْقَلَ = to burden (Form IV); مُثْقَل = overburdened

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
1.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'in their possession / with them / on their side' — a word marking presence-at or being-with, here belonging to 'them'.

parts.en: at / with / in the presence of

2.grammar: The locational word ʿinda ('at, with, in the keeping of') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). Its final -a is the fixed accusative form normal for this adverb of place. The pronoun is written -humu (with an extra u) to ease linking onto a following word that begins with the definite article.
2.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — at, near, in the presence/keeping of

3.meaning: 'The unseen / the hidden' — that which is beyond perception and out of reach of the senses; the realm of what is concealed and known fully only to Allah.
3.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative case (no nunation because al- makes it definite), the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified.
3.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be absent, hidden, concealed from sight

4.meaning: Means 'so they / then they' — the connector 'so/then' joined to the standalone pronoun 'they' (for a group of males or a mixed group). It draws a consequence and then names the subject.
4.grammar: The connecting particle fa- ('so/then', drawing a result or sequence from what precedes) attached to the detached subject pronoun hum ('they', masculine or mixed plural). As a standalone pronoun it has no case ending and serves as the subject of what follows.

5.meaning: 'They write / inscribe' — a present-tense verb of writing: to record, inscribe, or set down in letters; it can also carry the broader sense of prescribing or decreeing.
5.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the 'they/he' class, the -ū marks the masculine plural subject, and the -na ending signals the ordinary (indicative) present, 'they are writing.'
5.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing; recording, inscribing, prescribing

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
1.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
2.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.
2.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, will, intend

3.meaning: 'A scheme / plot / cunning stratagem' — the verbal noun naming the act of devising a crafty plan, often with hostile intent. It also intensifies the verb it accompanies ('scheme a real scheme').
3.grammar: A verbal noun in the indefinite accusative; the -an (tanwīn) marks an indefinite noun and is typical of an object that reinforces its own verb (a 'cognate' object, e.g. 'they schemed a scheme'). The nunation also signals 'a …' (indefinite).
3.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to scheme, plot, contrive

4.meaning: 'So those who / then they who' — a connective 'so/then' joined to a relative pronoun meaning 'those who' (a masculine plural group identified by what follows).
4.grammar: A connective fa- ('so/then') on a relative pronoun. 'Alladhīna means 'those who / the ones who' and introduces a description; it refers to a masculine plural group and its form does not change for case.
4.root: — (relative pronoun; no triliteral root)

5.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

6.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
6.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

7.meaning: Those in the plot / those contriving — a rhetorical question: are the disbelievers the ones plotting against the Prophet, or does God's plan surround them?

parts.en: those plotted against / those in the scheme (passive participle, plural)

7.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) of kāda (to plot, to scheme), in the definite sound masculine plural. Al-Makīdūn = those who are plotted against, or those who are subjected to scheming. The rhetorical question implies it is the disbelievers themselves who are in the trap.
7.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, to scheme; مَكِيد = one who is plotted against; المَكِيدُون = those schemed against

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
1.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

2.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
2.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

3.meaning: A god / an object of worship — a being taken as a deity and worshipped. As an indefinite noun it means 'a god' in the general sense.
3.grammar: A singular noun. The -un ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a god') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate.
3.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

4.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
4.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.
4.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, change

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: An exclamation declaring Allah utterly free of every flaw, partner, or imperfection — 'Glory be! / How perfect He is!' It is a noun of glorification used to affirm absolute transcendence and purity.
6.grammar: A verbal noun in the accusative case, marked by the -a ending; it functions as an exclamation typically followed by a noun in the genitive ('Glory be to …'). It conveys the act of declaring someone free of any defect.
6.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide; figuratively to declare free of imperfection

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
8.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

9.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
9.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
9.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: "That they should see / lest they see." A present-tense verb of seeing, perceiving with the eyes, or coming to realize.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, "they" (third-person masculine plural), from a root whose weak final letter drops away. The loss of the full "-ūna" plural ending (leaving "-aw") signals the subjunctive/jussive mood — used after particles meaning "that," "so that," or "lest," or in negation of the completed act. The silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.
2.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider

3.meaning: A fragment / a portion / a piece — if they see a piece of the sky falling, they would dismiss it as heaped-up clouds rather than believe.

parts.en: a fragment / a piece / a portion

3.grammar: Indefinite noun in the accusative case. Kisf (كِسْف) means a piece, portion, or fragment — specifically a broken piece of something. Here it refers to a fragment of the sky falling as a punishment.
3.root: ك-س-ف (k-s-f) — to break off, to eclipse; كِسْف = fragment, piece, portion

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: The sky or heaven — the canopy overhead; the expanse above the earth, also that which is elevated or raised over something. With the definite article it means 'the sky / the heaven'.
5.grammar: A noun with the definite article al- ('the'), in the genitive marked by the -i ending. (The 'l' of al- assimilates in sound into the following 's', a 'sun letter', though it is still written.) The genitive -i ending typically appears after a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
5.root: س-م-و (s-m-w) — height, loftiness; sky, heaven

6.meaning: Falling / dropping — the sky fragment described as falling down upon them.

parts.en: indefinite accusative ending (as ḥāl or adjective)

6.grammar: Active participle (ism fāʿil) on the pattern فَاعِل from root s-q-ṭ meaning 'to fall, to drop.' Indefinite accusative, functioning as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or adjective modifying kisf (a fragment falling).
6.root: س-ق-ط (s-q-ṭ) — to fall, to drop; سَاقِط = falling, dropping (active participle)

7.meaning: Verb meaning 'they say / they would say' — the act of speaking or uttering words, attributed to a masculine plural group.
7.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural ('they'). The dropped final 'nūn' (yaqūlū rather than yaqūlūna) shows it is in the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles meaning 'so that,' 'in order to,' or in conditional answers, rather than as a plain statement.

8.meaning: Clouds — the disbelievers, upon seeing a piece of sky falling, would mistake it for mere clouds, so deep is their denial.
8.grammar: Indefinite noun in the nominative case, predicate of the nominal sentence: hādhā saḥābun (this is clouds). Saḥāb (سَحَاب) is a collective noun meaning clouds — a mass of vapor in the sky.
8.root: س-ح-ب (s-ḥ-b) — to drag along; سَحَاب = clouds (that drag across the sky)

9.meaning: Heaped up / piled up — the disbelievers would call the falling sky fragment merely clouds heaped up, refusing to see it as divine punishment.

parts.en: heaped up / piled up / accumulated (passive participle)

9.grammar: Passive participle (ism mafʿūl) on the pattern مَفْعُول from root r-k-m meaning 'to pile up, to heap, to accumulate.' Indefinite nominative, adjective modifying saḥāb (clouds heaped up).
9.root: ر-ك-م (r-k-m) — to pile up, to heap; مَرْكُوم = heaped up, piled together

1.meaning: A command verb with an attached object, meaning 'so leave them / let them be / forsake them'. The underlying verb means to leave something alone, abandon it, or let it go.
1.grammar: fa- is 'so / then', drawing a consequence. dhar is an imperative (command) addressed to a single male ('you, leave!'); this very common verb is used only in present and command forms. The suffix -hum is the object 'them' (a group of males).
1.root: و-ذ-ر (w-dh-r) — to leave, let alone, forsake

2.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
2.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: They will encounter / they will meet — the disbelievers will encounter their punishment on the Day they are promised.

parts.en: they will meet / encounter / face (3rd masculine plural imperfect passive/active, Form III)

3.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), third person masculine plural from root l-q-y in Form III (lāqā = to meet, to encounter, to face). The final nūn is dropped due to the amil (contextual factor — following a conjunction with jussive effect or subjunctive). Form III implies facing something directly.
3.root: ل-ق-ي (l-q-y) — to meet, to encounter; لَاقَى = to meet, face (Form III); يُلَاقُوا = they encounter

4.meaning: Their Day — the Day of Judgment specifically appointed for them, the day they will face God's reckoning.
4.grammar: Noun yawm in the accusative case (temporal/ẓarf al-zamān) with the third-person masculine plural possessive suffix -hum (followed by a helping vowel -u before the next word). Yawmahum = 'their Day' — the day they have been promised and will be held accountable.
4.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — يَوْم = day; يَوْمَهُمُ = their day

5.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
5.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

6.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
6.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

7.meaning: They will faint / be thunderstruck — on the Day when the trumpet is blown, people will faint (or be struck unconscious) from the overwhelming terror.

parts.en: they will be thunderstruck / faint / struck unconscious (3rd plural passive imperfect)

7.grammar: Passive imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ majhūl), third person masculine plural from root ṣ-ʿ-q meaning 'to strike with a thunderbolt, to cause to faint, to overwhelm.' In context: yawma lā tughāsil al-kādhiba al-ṣaʿqah — or the verse referencing that day.
7.root: ص-ع-ق (ṣ-ʿ-q) — thunderbolt, to be struck down; يُصْعَقُون = they are thunderstruck/faint

1.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
1.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
1.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

2.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
2.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

3.meaning: A present/future verb meaning 'it avails, suffices, benefits, or makes free from need' — to be of use against something or to enrich and relieve someone of need. The root centres on richness, sufficiency, and being free of want.
3.grammar: An ongoing or future action. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'), and the form (causative pattern) carries the sense of 'to make sufficient' or 'to be of avail'. The final long -ī is the verb's own weak-root termination.
3.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be free of need, rich, sufficient

4.meaning: From them; away from them; concerning them. The preposition ʿan conveys moving away from, departing from, or 'on behalf of / concerning', combined with the pronoun 'them'.
4.grammar: A preposition joined to the attached pronoun -hum, 'them' (referring to a group, grammatically masculine plural). The preposition ʿan basically signals separation or removal ('away from'), and can also mean 'about/concerning' or 'on behalf of' depending on usage.
4.root: — (a preposition; no triliteral verbal root)

5.meaning: "Their plot / their scheme" — a cunning plan, stratagem, or covert plotting belonging to a group; deviousness aimed at someone.
5.grammar: A noun with the possessive suffix -hum ('their'). The -u ending is the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence (the doer). 'Kayd' denotes scheming or guile.
5.root: ك-ي-د (k-y-d) — to plot, scheme, contrive

6.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
6.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
6.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

7.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

8.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

9.meaning: To be helped, aided, or given victory — for support to be granted, especially against an adversary.
9.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, masculine plural 'they.' The yu- prefix is the third-person masculine imperfect marker; the passive sense ('they are being helped,' by an unnamed helper) comes from the internal vowelling rather than from the prefix itself. The -ūna ending marks a plural subject in the plain (indicative) present, used for an ongoing or general fact.
9.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, aid, grant victory

1.meaning: 'And indeed' / 'and truly' — the joining word 'wa' ('and') attached to the emphatic particle 'inna', which introduces a statement and strongly affirms it, adding certainty like 'surely' or 'indeed'.
1.grammar: A connective 'wa' ('and') plus 'inna', a particle of emphasis that opens a nominal sentence. 'Inna' puts its following noun (the subject) into the accusative case while strongly affirming the truth of the statement.

2.meaning: A compound meaning 'for those who' or 'belonging to those who'. It joins the preposition 'for/to' with a masculine plural relative pronoun ('those who'), introducing a clause that describes a group of people by something they do or possess.
2.grammar: The prefix 'li-' is a preposition meaning 'for', 'to', or expressing ownership/benefit ('belonging to'). The relative pronoun is 'alladhīna' ('those who'), but when 'li-' attaches to it the connecting hamza of 'al-' drops out and the two lām sounds merge into one doubled lām, so the form is written and read 'lilladhīna' rather than 'li-alladhīna'. 'alladhīna' has a fixed shape and does not change for case.

3.meaning: 'They wronged / did injustice / acted unjustly'. The core idea is putting something out of its rightful place — oppression, transgression, or wronging oneself or others.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb with the plural subject ending -ū ('they', masculine/mixed group), referring to a completed action done by many. The -ū suffix is written with a silent 'alif' after it. It states that a group performed the act of wronging.
3.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — to wrong, oppress; to put a thing out of its proper place

4.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
4.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.
4.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to torment, punish, chastise

5.meaning: An adverb/preposition meaning 'apart from, other than, short of, below.' It points to something falling outside or beneath a named thing — 'aside from X' or 'lesser than X'.
5.grammar: An invariable adverbial noun used like a preposition. It carries a fixed -a ending and governs a following noun in the genitive, yielding the sense 'other than …' or 'short of …'.
5.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be below, lesser, or beneath

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: But; however; rather. A particle of correction or contrast that cancels or qualifies a preceding statement and introduces what is actually the case.
7.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') joined to the emphatic particle lākinna. Lākinna belongs to the 'inna family: it governs the noun that follows it, putting it in the accusative case, and adds a sense of firm contrast — 'but in fact …'.

8.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger portion of a group.
8.grammar: An elative/comparative noun ('more/most, the greater number') on the 'afʿal' pattern. The -a ending marks the accusative case, the form used when the word is a verb's object. The attached -hum ('them') is in the possessive role, completing the sense 'the most of them'.

9.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
9.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

10.meaning: They know, have knowledge, are aware. Expresses ongoing or habitual knowing held by a group of males (or a mixed group).
10.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they' (a group of males). The full -ūna ending (rather than a shortened -ū) marks the indicative mood, signaling a plain statement of fact: 'they (do) know.'

1.meaning: And be patient / endure steadfastly / persevere — sabr is the disciplined restraint of the self: bearing hardship calmly, holding firm, and not giving way to impatience or despair. The leading wa is the connective 'and.'
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a single person, 'be patient!', carrying the connective wa ('and'). The clipped, vowel-less ending is the normal shape of the singular command form.
1.root: ص-ب-ر (ṣ-b-r) — to be patient, endure, restrain oneself, persevere

2.meaning: For the command / decree of God — the Prophet is commanded to be patient, awaiting and under the judgment of his Lord.
2.grammar: Prepositional phrase: li + genitive noun ḥukm. Li-ḥukmi rabbika = 'for the judgment of your Lord' — be patient awaiting God's decree. Ḥukm (حُكْم) means judgment, ruling, command, or decree.
2.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to rule; حُكْم = judgment, decree, command

3.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
3.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
3.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

4.meaning: A two-part opener meaning roughly 'then/so, truly You …': a connecting 'then/so' joined to an emphatic particle that asserts what follows with certainty, plus an attached 'You.' The emphatic particle (inna) strongly affirms the statement, like saying 'indeed' or 'it is certainly the case that.'
4.grammar: A particle cluster, not a verb. fa- is a connector ('then, so, and thus'). inna is an emphatic/affirming particle that places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative; here that pronoun is the attached -ka ('you,' one male), the topic being emphasized. There is no tense or case ending of its own.
4.root: — (particles; no root)

5.meaning: 'With/under Our eyes' — an idiom for being kept under loving, protective oversight and supervision; the literal sense is the organs of sight.
5.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with/by/under'. Because it is a preposition, the following noun takes the genitive -i ending. The plural noun aʿyun ('eyes') is then linked to the attached pronoun -nā ('our'), which serves as a possessor.
5.root: ع-ي-ن ('-y-n) — eye; by extension a spring of water and the essence of a thing.

6.meaning: And declare Allah's perfection — to glorify, to proclaim Him utterly free of every flaw or imperfection, exalting and praising Him; the command to do so.

parts.en: glorify / declare free of all imperfection

6.grammar: A command (imperative) verb in the intensive (Form II, فَعَّلَ) pattern, addressed to one male. The vowel-less final -ḥ is the clipped imperative ending, the bare command form telling 'you' to do the action.
6.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to glorify, to declare free of all imperfection

7.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with the praise of' — joining the preposition 'with/by' to the noun 'praise.' Ḥamd is praise mingled with gratitude and admiration directed to one who deserves it.
7.grammar: A preposition 'bi-' ('with/by') attached to the noun 'praise.' The '-i' ending is genitive, which here follows the preposition and also links 'praise' to a following word ('praise OF …').
7.root: ح-م-د (ḥ-m-d) — to praise (with gratitude and admiration)

8.meaning: A noun with an attached pronoun meaning 'your Lord' — the Lord/Master/Sustainer of a single person addressed. Rabb conveys an owner who creates, nurtures, sustains, and governs all that is under His care.
8.grammar: The noun rabb ('Lord, Sustainer') carries the -i genitive vowel, which typically appears when the noun follows a preposition or is itself possessed by a following noun ('… of your Lord'). The suffix -ka means 'your', addressed to a single male.
8.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — lordship; to nurture, sustain, master

9.meaning: 'Time / moment / period when' — a point or span of time; often used to mean 'at the time that …' or 'when'.
9.grammar: A noun meaning 'a time / moment'. The '-a' ending here functions adverbially, giving the sense 'at the time when …', and is also the form taken as the object of a verb. It frequently introduces a clause and behaves like the conjunction 'when'.

10.meaning: You arise / you stand — a command or temporal reference to the time when the Prophet stands up from sleep (at night vigil) to glorify God.

parts.en: you arise / you stand up (2nd masculine singular imperfect)

10.grammar: Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), second person masculine singular from root q-w-m meaning 'to stand, to arise, to get up.' Indicative mood marked by the final ḍamma. In context (ḥīna taqūmu = when you arise), it refers to the Prophet's rising for the night prayer.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; تَقُوم = you stand/arise

1.meaning: A connector meaning 'and', joined to the preposition 'from / of', introducing a portion or origin — 'and from' or 'and among'.
1.grammar: Two particles: wa- ('and') plus the preposition min ('from, of, among'). Min normally appears as 'min', but its final vowel shifts to 'mina' when the next word begins with the definite article, simply to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.
1.root: — (particles)

2.meaning: The night — the period of darkness from sunset to dawn.
2.grammar: Prefix 'al-' = 'the' (its 'l' merges with the word's initial 'l', said al-layl). A noun for night-time. The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically used after a preposition or to link to a preceding noun ('… OF the night').
2.root: ل-ي-ل (l-y-l) — night, nightfall

3.meaning: So glorify Him / so exalt Him — the surah closes with a command to glorify God at the setting of the stars, completing the cycle of glorification across the day.

parts.en: glorify / exalt / praise (2nd singular imperative, Form II)

3.grammar: Consequence particle fa + imperative verb (ṣīghat al-amr) from root s-b-ḥ in Form II (sabbaḥa = to glorify intensively, to declare God's transcendence). Second person masculine singular imperative with the third-person masculine singular object suffix -hu (referring to God).
3.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim, to glorify; سَبَّحَ = to glorify (Form II); فَسَبِّحْهُ = so glorify Him!

4.meaning: And after / and at the setting of — glorify your Lord at the setting of the stars, i.e., in the predawn and nighttime hours.

parts.en: the setting / the turning away / the receding (verbal noun)

4.grammar: Verbal noun (maṣdar) of Form IV of d-b-r meaning 'the turning away, the going behind, the setting.' Accusative case (temporal adverbial): wa-idbāra l-nujūmi = 'and at the setting of the stars.' Refers to glorifying God at the end of the night.
4.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — to follow behind, to set; إِدْبَار = the setting, the turning away (Form IV maṣdar)

5.meaning: The stars — glorify God at the setting of the stars, i.e., in the hours before dawn when the stars are retreating.
5.grammar: Definite noun in the genitive case (after the genitive construction idbāra l-nujūm = the setting of the stars). Al-Nujūm (النُّجُوم) is the broken plural of najm (نَجْم), meaning stars.
5.root: ن-ج-م (n-j-m) — to appear, to rise; نَجْم = star; نُجُوم = stars (plural)
